newsitem.title: USA: Diodes shows optimism over outlook.
newsitem.headline: Diodes shows optimism over outlook.

text.p: Diodes Inc said Wednesday though its third quarter sales and earnings fell from the year-ago quarter, the figures rose from 1996's second quarter, boosting optimism over its business outlook.

Revenues for the quarter dropped 6.3 percent to $14.4 million from the year ago's $15.4 million, Net income was $755,000 versus $1.3 million last year, and primary earnings per share were $0.14 compared with $0.24.
In the second quarter ended June 30, Diodes reported net income of $555,000, or $0.11 a share, on sales of $13.5 million.

"Provided industry conditions continue to improve, we are cautiously optimistic that we will continue to see further improvements in the company's revenues and earnings per share," David Lin, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Lin said Diodes' gross profit as a percentage of sales was lower than hoped, due to industry-wide pricing pressure and greater inventory reserves recorded by the company. However, Diodes has reduced total inventory by 13.8 percent since the year's start and has cut overhead costs.
Diodes makes discrete semiconductor products for auto, electronics/computing and telecommunications industries.
